criterion.title: Declared royalty-free patent commitment
criterion.definition: An attributable holder declaration or published commitment explicitly offers royalty-free implementation of the selected profile for applicable claims under the declaring holder's control. A recorded direct holder declaration is admissible for every project; publication or registry entry is reported separately, not required for Yes. State attribution, scope, conditions and publication status. This assesses the declared policy, not execution or enforceability of a patent license, third-party patent clearance, or copyright permission. An express patent grant attached to the selected implementation is admissible within its stated Work or contributor-version scope; it is not a promise covering every independent reimplementation. The same holder-bounded rule applies to direct declarations and public grants.
criterion.research_action: Obtain a dated attributable holder declaration or applicable public grant; identify scope, conditions and publication status. Do not infer a commitment solely from open development, copyright licensing or IETF participation.

criterion.title: Let each operator enforce local access and resource priorities
criterion.definition: Each transport scope can administer its resources and establish and enforce local access and priority conditions, respecting agreements with participants, without requiring one uniform policy throughout the network. Identify the scope, policy owner, controlled resources and enforcement point. Scopes may be adjacent or nested; recursive layers and hidden internal topology are not required. Configurable local preferences alone do not suffice without control of the relevant resources. F36 separately assesses participant-requested service quality, and F37 response to congestion. Local autonomy does not imply unlimited resources, arbitrary violation of agreements or absence of higher-level constraints.
criterion.method: Primary evidence for the selected composition; identify mechanism, scope and implementation limits
criterion.research_action: Identify independently administered transport scopes, local access/priority policy and resource enforcement. Explain how different local conditions can coexist along a communication. Do not require nesting, topology abstraction or RINA-style layers. Distinguish local policy authority from the ability merely to request QoS.

cells.reason: The author states that each PRP aggregator sees its own adjacencies and transiting clients. Each adjacency represents an interface with control-plane priority, and transiting participants can negotiate access priorities within its resource budget. Together with previously clarified autonomous adjacency scheduling, this establishes local resource administration and negotiated access/priority conditions at each aggregator without requiring a uniform policy along the complete trajectory. The architectural Yes credits independent transport scopes, not an inferred nested-domain service.

cells.reason: Each GNUnet operator configures local ATS network-scope bandwidth budgets. CORE also schedules according to message priority and available bandwidth. Operators can enforce different budgets and priorities at adjacent relay scopes without a uniform network-wide policy.
